cards.question: Step 1-2-3 Plus?
cards.answer: 1 casualty: approach normally. 2: approach with caution. 3+: do not approach — withdraw, report, isolate. Plus: get people out, disrobe, decontaminate.

cards.question: Classic clues of a chemical incident?
cards.answer: Multiple casualties, similar symptoms, no trauma; odors/mists/liquids; dead animals/vegetation; people fleeing from one point.

cards.question: DOT hazard classes 1–9?
cards.answer: 1 Explosives, 2 Gases, 3 Flammable liquids, 4 Flammable solids, 5 Oxidizers, 6 Toxic/infectious, 7 Radioactive, 8 Corrosives, 9 Miscellaneous.

cards.question: ERG page colors?
cards.answer: Yellow: by ID number. Blue: by name. Orange: guides. Green: isolation & protective action distances (TIH).

cards.question: NFPA 704 colors?
cards.answer: Blue health, Red flammability, Yellow instability, White special hazards; 0–4 severity.

cards.question: PPE Level C?
cards.answer: Air-purifying respirator + splash suit — known agent, adequate O2.

cards.question: Single most effective decon step?
cards.answer: Removing clothing — removes most external contamination (~80–90% often quoted).

cards.question: Dry vs wet decon?
cards.answer: Dry (blot/wipe) is default for most exposures; wet (high-volume, low-pressure water) for caustics, visible liquid contamination, or symptomatic patients.

cards.question: Where does EMS without HazMat training work?
cards.answer: Cold zone — receive patients after decon.
